step1_figure.circuit_type: Common-Source Amplifier with Current Source Load
step1_figure.description: A common-source amplifier (M1) utilizing a PMOS current source (M2) as its load to achieve high voltage gain. The complex bias circuit (SUB_1) generates the necessary gate voltage for the PMOS load.

low_frequency_gain.description: Open-loop low-frequency voltage gain of the amplifier.

equation.explanation: Gain is the transconductance of the input device multiplied by the total output resistance.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming I_D = 20uA, W/L=10. g_m1 = sqrt(2*270u*10*20u) = 328uS. r_o1 = r_o2 = 1/(0.1*20u) = 500kOhm. R_out = 250kOhm. A_v = 328uS * 250kOhm = 82 V/V = 38.3 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Gain depends heavily on channel length and exact bias current, typically 30-40 dB for a single-stage CS amp in 130nm.

output_pole.description: Dominant pole frequency at the output node.

equation.explanation: The pole is determined by the output resistance and the total capacitance at the output node.
equation.assumptions: tau_out = R_out * C_out, where C_out is dominated by the 1pF load capacitor.

sky130_expected.calculation: R_out = 250 kOhm, C_out = 1 pF. f_out = 1 / (2 * pi * 250e3 * 1e-12) = 636 kHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by the 1pF load and the output resistance of the transistors.

right_half_plane_zero.description: Frequency of the right-half plane zero caused by C_gd1.

equation.explanation: Feedforward path through the gate-drain capacitance creates a RHP zero.
equation.assumptions: C_gd1 is the overlap capacitance of M1.

sky130_expected.calculation: g_m1 = 328 uS. Assuming C_gd1 ~ 2 fF. f_z = 328e-6 / (2 * pi * 2e-15) = 26 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: RHP zero is typically at very high frequencies, well beyond the unity gain frequency.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC operating point, AC gain, bandwidth, and transient response of the CS amplifier.
